what_it_does: Modern processors speed up execution by predicting which way a program's if-else branches will go before they are actually evaluated — a feature called branch prediction. Spectre-style attacks exploit this by tricking the processor into speculatively executing code it should not, briefly exposing secret data in side channels before the mis-speculation is caught and rolled back. BPUFuzzer is an automated testing tool that searches for such transient-execution vulnerabilities specifically in RISC-V processors (an open-source chip instruction set that is increasingly used in research and industry). It generates test programs by analyzing the control-flow structure of code — the graph of all possible paths through branches — and uses anomaly detection to flag cases where the hardware behaved differently than expected, hinting at a potential exploit. A fitness-and-coverage metric guides the fuzzer toward interesting corner cases rather than exploring randomly.
